metaDescription: Seven battery lawn mowers compared on deck width, self propelled drive, battery voltage and Ah, runtime, mulching and bagging, with picks by lawn size.
expertTake: The EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 is our top pick for a self propelled 21 inch deck, strong torque and a long stated runtime from its larger battery. The Greenworks 48V 17 inch is the value pick for a small to medium yard where a light poly deck matters more than width. Skip a cordless mower if your lawn is more than about an acre or very wet and thick, because runtime and battery cost start to work against you.
introParagraphs: A cordless lawn mower replaces the gas engine with a brushless motor and a lithium ion battery, which removes the pull cord, the fuel and the oil changes. The result is a quieter, lighter machine that starts with a button and needs little more than blade care.

Runtime is the constraint, and it depends on battery size, grass height and wetness. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for lawn size and terrain rather than by voltage alone.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 21 inch self propelled cordless mower, up to 100 minutes

specList.label: Runtime
specList.value: Up to 100 minutes per the listing

specList.label: Torque
specList.value: Up to 7.0 ft-lbs of cutting torque

products.description:
The LM2134SP-2 is a 21 inch self propelled mower that the maker says delivers up to 7.0 ft-lbs of cutting torque and up to 100 minutes of runtime on its battery. A longer runtime claim comes from a larger battery in the kit, not a different mower.

Self propelled drive removes the effort of pushing a heavy deck uphill, and the 21 inch width cuts fewer passes than a 14 or 17 inch deck. Against the EGO LM2135SP, this kit has a longer stated runtime and higher cost tier. Against the Greenworks 60V 21 inch push mower, the EGO adds drive and a brand with a deep accessory line.

Store the battery indoors at moderate temperatures and clean the underside of the deck after each mow. Sharpen or replace the blade once a season, and rinse grass from the deck so it does not rust. Owners often add a second battery for very large lawns, which turns one charge into a full afternoon of mowing.

products.description:
The LM2135SP is the same style of mower as the LM2134SP-2 with a smaller battery in the kit and a stated runtime of up to 60 minutes. That is plenty for a medium lawn, and it costs less.

If your yard takes under an hour to mow, this kit saves money without changing the machine. If your yard is larger, the LM2134SP-2 or a second battery is worth it. Against the Greenworks 48V 17 inch, the EGO has a wider deck and self propulsion at a higher tier.

Keep the battery out of direct sun and avoid leaving it in a hot garage. Wash the deck with a hose after mowing and check the blade for dents. If you later need more time, buying a larger battery separately is cheaper than replacing the whole mower.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21 inch push electric mower kit, 5Ah battery, mulch, bag, steel deck
products.description:
The Greenworks 60V push mower has a 21 inch steel deck, a 5Ah battery and an IPX4 rating, meaning it resists splashing water. The listing says 60V delivers 50 percent more torque than a 40V mower and a blade speed of 3200 RPM.

It does not include self propulsion, so it suits flat, medium lawns. A steel deck is heavier than poly but resists impacts better. Against the Greenworks 48V 17 inch, it has a larger deck and more power. Against the EGO self propelled models, it is lighter in the price tier and simpler.

Rinse the underside after mowing and keep the battery dry. Replace the blade when it dulls. Owners of steel deck models say a quick scrape after each mow prevents the slow rust that eats the underside.

specList.label: Deck

products.description:
The Greenworks 48V uses two 24V batteries in series, with a 17 inch rust resistant poly deck that the listing says is 40 percent lighter than steel. Two 4Ah batteries and a dual port charger are included.

The poly deck makes the mower easy to push and lift, which suits smaller yards and users who do not want a heavy machine. The narrower 17 inch cut means more passes on a large lawn. Against the WORX 14 inch, it has a wider deck and bigger batteries. Against the Greenworks 60V, it is lighter but less powerful.

Charge batteries after use and store them indoors. Wipe the poly deck after each mow. The series connection of two packs means both must be charged and seated before it starts.

products.name: NovorikX 60V 21 inch self propelled cordless mower, 2 x 5.0Ah batteries, 1200 W brushless
products.description:
The NovorikX offers a 1200 W brushless motor, a 21 inch steel deck, self propelled drive and two 5.0Ah batteries on a 60V platform. Two batteries mean you can swap one during a long mow, which is a real advantage.

It sits at a lower tier than the EGO mowers while offering similar headline features. The tradeoff is brand history and parts support, and a young battery platform has less accessory support. Against the Greenworks 60V push, it adds self propulsion and a second battery.

Charge the spare while you mow and keep the deck clean. Check the drive controls and blade for wear. With little accessory support, treat the battery as a single purpose pack for this mower.

products.name: WORX 20V 14 inch cordless 2 in 1 mower WG733.1, brushless, cut to edge
products.description:
The WORX WG733.1 is a compact 14 inch brushless mower with a cut to edge design that allows closer trimming along walls and fences. It converts between bagging and mulching.

A 14 inch deck is best suited to a small yard or a townhouse lawn, where manoeuvrability matters more than width. Against the Greenworks 17 inch, it is smaller and lighter. Against the Litheli 14 inch, it offers a more recognised brand and an edge focused design.

Share the WORX 20V battery with other tools in the line. Clean grass from the deck after each mow. A light mower like this is also the easiest to carry up a step or into a shed.

products.name: Litheli 14 inch cordless mower, brushless, 5.0Ah battery, 5 position height
products.description:
The Litheli is a compact 14 inch brushless mower with a 5.0Ah battery and a single lever, five position height adjustment. It targets users who want to ditch gas for a small lawn.

A single lever for height is easier than adjusting four wheels, which suits casual mowing. The 14 inch deck and a single battery limit it to small lawns. Against the WORX, it lacks the edge design but costs less. Against the Greenworks 17 inch, it is smaller and lighter.

Charge after each use and clean the deck. Store the battery indoors. If your lawn grows quickly in spring, raise the deck a notch so the motor is not overloaded.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Deck width sets how many passes you make. A 14 inch deck suits under a quarter acre, a 17 inch deck suits a medium yard and a 21 inch deck suits larger lawns. A wider deck is heavier, so match width to the area and your strength. The usual buyer mistake is choosing voltage while ignoring the Ah rating and the wattage of the pack.

Voltage describes power and amp hours describe capacity. A 60V 5Ah pack holds more energy than a 20V 4Ah pack. Runtime claims, like up to 100 minutes on the EGO or up to 60 minutes on the smaller kit, depend on grass height and wetness. See our guide on battery voltage and amp hours for the maths. Mow when the grass is dry and no more than a third of the blade height is removed, which saves runtime.

Self propelled drive, as on the EGO and NovorikX, takes effort out of hills and thick grass. Push mowers such as the Greenworks 60V are lighter and cheaper but demand more work. For slopes or a large lawn, self propulsion is worth it. Check the weight of the mower you can lift, since you will carry it to the shed and up a curb.

Steel decks are durable but heavy and can rust if left wet. Poly decks, like the Greenworks 48V, are 40 percent lighter and rust free but less impact resistant. Choose by how much weight you can handle. Self propelled units usually have a speed dial, so look for one that matches your walking pace.

Mulching returns fine clippings to the lawn, bagging keeps it tidy and side discharge handles tall grass. Most models here offer two or three modes. Check that the bag capacity suits your lawn. Mulching uses more power than side discharge, so expect shorter runtime when mulching thick grass.

A mower is a long term buy and the battery platform decides what other tools you can use. EGO and Greenworks have broad ranges, WORX shares 20V packs with many tools. A second battery, as in the NovorikX kit, extends mowing time. Look for a folding handle if storage space is tight, since cordless mowers store upright.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lawn fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 14, 17 and 21 inch decks against typical lawn sizes. We favoured a match between deck width and area. Owner feedback patterns about battery fade and charger reliability shaped our view of long term cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at voltage, Ah ratings and stated runtimes such as 100 minutes on the EGO kit. We treated runtime as a manufacturer claim and did not run our own timed mows. We discounted runtime claims that did not state the grass condition.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed self propelled drive on the EGO and NovorikX against push models. We also considered deck weight. Where two kits shared a mower body we compared batteries and nothing else.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed steel versus poly decks, IPX4 on the Greenworks and mulch, bag and discharge options. Durable decks scored higher. We checked whether chargers are included and how fast they charge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ecosystem and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered battery platforms, included batteries and owner feedback patterns about battery life. Broad platforms scored higher. Parts availability for blades and batteries counted for the brand.

maintenance.why: Wet clippings cake and rust the deck. Rinse or scrape when the battery is removed.
A dull blade tears grass and drains battery. Replace if it is dented.
Heat and cold shorten battery life. Store at partial charge in a dry place.
Dirt jams height adjusters. Clean and lubricate lightly.
Clippings clog discharge and reduce airflow. Clear before each mow.

faq.q: How big a lawn can a cordless mower handle?
faq.a: A single 5Ah battery typically handles a small to medium lawn. Larger lawns need a bigger battery like the EGO 100 minute kit or a spare battery. Many owners say the quiet motor is the biggest everyday benefit, since you can mow early without annoying neighbours.
Not on its own. Voltage describes power, and amp hours describe capacity. Watt hours give the full picture, so compare both. Keep spare blades on hand so you can swap one quickly.
For hills or large lawns, yes. For small flat lawns, a push mower is lighter and cheaper. Charge the battery at room temperature for the longest life.
It is not ideal, since wet clippings clog the deck and drain the battery. An IPX4 rating tolerates splashes but not heavy rain. Fold the handle only as the manual describes to avoid cable damage.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Many last several seasons with proper care, with capacity fading gradually. Store them at partial charge indoors. Mulching kits help return nutrients to the lawn, which can reduce fertiliser needs.

faq.q: Is a cordless mower as powerful as gas?
faq.a: For typical residential lawns, high voltage models are comparable, though thick wet grass and very large lawns still favour gas. Wear closed shoes and eye protection when mowing.
